history.text: Heavy rain brought hills down in Launglon, killing people and destroying hundreds of acres of orchards.
Launglon residents recall large landslides like these.
At Pa Nyit a slide buried about 100 houses and 61 people died in the mud, villagers say.

storm.en: 21 Sep: Thailand's meteorological department warns of heavy to very heavy rain, flash floods and landslides for 23–27 Sep as a low moves in from central Vietnam.
26 Sep: the low, crossing Cambodia and Thailand, meets a strong south-west monsoon over the Andaman Sea. Record rain floods Bangkok; heavy rain at Dawei.
The Tanintharyi range lifts the moist monsoon air and wrings the rain out on its Andaman-facing side (orographic lift).
Hillsides already soaked by the monsoon take in more water than they can hold; pore pressure rises and slopes fail.
28 Sep: DMH expects the low to strengthen into a depression and move north and north-west, across the Gulf of Mottama towards the Ayeyarwady delta.
28 Sep: DMH records 13.62 in (346 mm) at Dawei, a second record in two days. Rain stops over most of the area from midday.
DMH has warned that a strong El Niño set in this September, bringing erratic rain, heat, storms and drought.

sites.match_note: Taken as MIMU's U Yin Kan (ဥယျာဉ်ကမ်း), 3 km from Aw Gyi in the same tract; no U Yin Kwin in MIMU.

reports.text: Travellers say the rising river is over the Myeik–Tanintharyi road here.

sites.mm: လယ်တောင်ယာ

reports.text: About 5 ft of water on the Tanintharyi–Kawthoung road: vehicles cannot pass, and motorcycles are ferried across on rafts.

sites.mimu_mm: လယ်တောင်ယာ

sites.match_note: MIMU spells it လေညာ (Lay Nyar), as the post itself does once; Htaung Yaik village tract.

reports.text: The Lay Hnya river rose into the village on 27 Sep: roads and low-lying houses under water, and residents of the low ground moving up the pagoda hill. Knee-deep in the village centre, with rain still falling on the evening of 28 Sep.

references.note: Southern end of the affected stretch of the Launglon peninsula, home to one of the 'nine Shins' pagodas. Not in MIMU village points, so not mapped.
Thai–Myanmar border crossing at the far end of the Dawei–Htee Khee road.

references.mm: ထားဝယ် အထူးစီးပွားရေးဇုန်
references.note: Its condition was still being checked on 27 Sep.

incidents.text: The hill between Launglon town and Nyin Maw collapsed on the morning of 27 Sep, burying the road in earth, rock and trees. It stopped the rescue convoy at about 2:30 pm; the alternative route by Pyin Htein was under water a person's height deep.
incidents.match_note: Hill not in MIMU. Placed midway between Launglon town and Nyin Maw, then moved onto the nearest MIMU road.

incidents.mm: ပြင်းထိန်ရွာလမ်း
incidents.text: The detour around the Poe Zar Pin slide through Pyin Htein was under water about a person's height deep.

incidents.en: Road closed at Ka Myaw Gyi
incidents.text: Vehicles barred from Ka Myaw Gyi, at the Dawei–Launglon boundary, onward; flooding held up rescue teams there on the morning of 27 Sep.
The road from Kyauk Ni Maw to Shin Maw is destroyed and impassable.

incidents.en: Kayin Gyi bridge and roads destroyed
incidents.mm: ကရင်ကြီး တံတား
incidents.text: The second slide destroyed the village bridge and roads; the road by the bridge is cut.

incidents.mm: ဆန်းချီတံတား
incidents.text: Water over the San Chi bridge on 27 Sep; submerged by 28 Sep.

incidents.mm: ထားဝယ်-ထီးခီးလမ်း
incidents.text: With Pa Kar Ri under water, vehicles cannot pass on the Dawei–Htee Khee border road.

incidents.en: Slide on the road near Tha Yet Ngoke
incidents.mm: သရက်ငုတ်
incidents.text: A landslide on the main road leaves one lane; vehicles pass one at a time.

incidents.mm: ကညင်ချောင်း တံတား
incidents.text: The bridge on Union Road No. 8 at Ka Nyin Chaung was destroyed, cutting the Dawei–Myeik road.

incidents.mm: ထားဝယ်-မြိတ်လမ်း
incidents.text: 2–4 ft of water on the road on 27 Sep: vehicles from Dawei turned back at Thin Kyun, vehicles from Myeik were stranded near Pe Det and beyond Palauk. By 28 Sep some stretches were 6–8 ft deep.

incidents.mm: သာရဘွင် တံတား
incidents.text: The bridge linking Thar Ra Bwin and the east-bank village is under water.

incidents.en: Slide on the road to Pa Nyit
incidents.mm: လောင်းလုံး–ပညစ်လမ်း
incidents.text: Photos show a slide across the road between Launglon town and Pa Nyit.
incidents.match_note: Placed midway between Launglon town and Pa Nyit, then moved onto the nearest MIMU road.

incidents.en: Slide on the road to Kan Pa Ni
incidents.mm: ပညစ်–ကမ်းပနီလမ်း
incidents.text: A second slide between Pa Nyit and Kan Pa Ni. Shan Maw, Pein Ne Chaung and Kyone Ga Nan, reached through Pa Nyit, are cut off.
incidents.match_note: Placed midway between Pa Nyit and Kan Pa Ni, then moved onto the nearest MIMU road.

incidents.mm: ဗျောတောဝ–ဇလွန်းလမ်း
incidents.text: Cars and motorcycles could not get through between Byaw Taw Wa and Za Lun, east of Dawei, on the evening of 28 Sep.

incidents.en: Two rope bridges destroyed at Mei Ke
incidents.mm: မယ်ကဲ ကြိုးတံတား
incidents.text: Two rope bridges at Mei Ke, Thayetchaung, were destroyed.

incidents.en: Slide debris between Nyin Maw and Ti Zit
incidents.mm: ညင်းမော်–တီဇစ်လမ်း
incidents.text: Earth and rock from the slides of 26 Sep block the hill road from Nyin Maw over to Ti Zit; residents want it cleared so the village can be reached.
incidents.match_note: Placed midway between Nyin Maw and Ti Zit, then moved onto the nearest MIMU road.

incidents.en: Bridges down on the road to Shin Maw
incidents.text: Many bridges are destroyed on the road from Kyauk Ni Maw down to Shin Maw.
incidents.match_note: Placed at Kyauk Wut Pyin, on that road; the posts do not say which bridges.

incidents.mm: မြိတ်-တနင်္သာရီလမ်း
incidents.text: The rising river is over the road at Aw Gyi and U Yin Kwin, travellers say.

incidents.mm: တနင်္သာရီ-ကော့သောင်းလမ်း
incidents.text: About 5 ft of water on the road at Lel Taung Yar; vehicles cannot pass and motorcycles cross on rafts.

incidents.mm: ကျောက်ဆင်
incidents.text: About 100 junta troops entered Kyauk Sin village tract, which includes landslide-hit Kayin Gyi. They said they had come to help but stayed at Kyauk Sin, and residents fled.

incidents.en: Junta column in the Dawei SEZ
incidents.text: A column of about 300 has been in Ya Laing, Pu Gaw Zun and Thit Toe Htaung, in the Dawei Special Economic Zone, since 23 Sep, after a clash near Pein Shaung on 25 Sep. Residents fled into the storm. Resistance forces say they have pulled back to avoid fighting during the disaster.
incidents.match_note: Placed at Ya Laing, the first of the three villages named.

rescue.en: Emergency rescue teams leave Dawei for Launglon.
Held up by flooding at Ka Myaw Gyi; the red-level villages are out of reach.
Reach Tha Byar and clear slide debris from the road near Pyin Sa Thi Maw and the monastery.
Stopped by the Poe Zar Pin slide. The detour is flooded; the teams appeal for backhoes and tractors to dig through.
An advance team walks round the slide on forest paths and reaches Kadet Nge Htein; search and rescue begins.
Furthest point reached. Villages further south, Taw Kye, Tha Kyet Taw, Ra Be, Za Lut and Nyaw Pyin, have had no help.
Backhoes have cleared the road as far as Nyin Maw, the teams' base and supply point since 28 Sep. Kyauk Ni Maw and the villages beyond still have no rescue team.

road.t: Backhoes have cleared the road only as far as Nyin Maw. Slides still block the hill road to Ti Zit and nearly every village further south.

bridge.t: Many bridges destroyed on the road from Kyauk Ni Maw down to Shin Maw.

comms.t: Kyauk Ni Maw reachable only through villagers who find a signal; Ti Zit's phone tower is running out of fuel.

rescue.t: A dozen-strong advance team at Kadet Nge Htein since 28 Sep; no team has reached Kyauk Ni Maw, Ti Zit, Za Lut or Nyaw Pyin.

supplies.t: Ti Zit's 1,000-plus people live on shop stocks; 200-plus at Kyauk Ni Maw's monastery need food and medicine.

rows.sub: Ka Myaw Gyi to Nyin Maw

road.t: Water fell on the evening of 28 Sep at Ka Myaw Gyi, Way Di, Min Yat, Tha Byar and in Launglon town.

rescue.t: Teams based at Nyin Maw, where relief supplies are collected and handed out.

supplies.t: Food, clothes and above all drinking water: the slides wrecked the village wells.

road.t: Slides on the road either side of Pa Nyit.

bridge.t: Kayin Gyi's bridge and village roads destroyed.

comms.t: Shan Maw, Pein Ne Chaung and Kyone Ga Nan, beyond Pa Nyit, cut off and out of contact.

rescue.t: Teams from Maungmagan working the Kayin Gyi and Kan Pa Ni side.

supplies.t: Kayin Gyi's residents in the monastery, short of food.

road.t: Water falling in the wards on the morning of 29 Sep; people back home cleaning up.

power.t: Off since 27 Sep; still off at midday on 29 Sep.

comms.t: Some phone lines down until at least the evening of 28 Sep.

rescue.t: Residents of seven wards moved out overnight on 27 Sep; the Red Cross giving health care.

supplies.t: 600-plus people in five monasteries need food, clothes and medicine.

road.t: Impassable between Byaw Taw Wa and Za Lun on 28 Sep; Pa Kar Ri under water; one lane past a slide at Tha Yet Ngoke.

supplies.t: Pa Kar Ri tract villagers in monasteries need food.

road.t: Ka Nyin Chaung bridge on Union Road No. 8 destroyed; the Dawei–Myeik road is cut.

bridge.t: Ka Nyin Chaung bridge; two rope bridges at Mei Ke; rope bridges in the Taung Pyauk area.

power.t: Still off on 29 Sep, after the water fell.

comms.t: Phone lines down because the power is off.

rescue.t: Only a local charity, with no boats; the district's teams are all in Launglon.

supplies.t: Drinking water, food and clothes, and help clearing silt. Wells flooded; the town market's food lost.

rows.sub: Myeik District, south on the highway

road.t: Flooded stretches between Palaw, Palauk and Pala; vehicles stranded.
5 ft of water on the Tanintharyi–Kawthoung road at Lel Taung Yar; the Myeik road under water at Aw Gyi.

bridge.t: Low roads and bridges under water in Ta Ku, Thar Ra Bwin and Thein Daw; people use boats and rafts.

comms.t: Phone lines cut, on and off.

timeline.en: Hills in southern Launglon begin collapsing, as far as Kyet Lut.
Heavy rain sets in over Launglon and keeps falling into the night.
A landslide buries houses and people at Kyauk Ni Maw.
People push motorcycles through floodwater on tractors; by night every road is under water and the bridges are submerged.
Villagers pull an elderly person and two children from the slide at Kyauk Ni Maw; the ground is still moving.
Thirteen people go missing in the Kadet Nge Htein slide.
At Nyaw Pyin the hill 'roars like an aeroplane', then collapses; neighbours dig out an old woman. (A 28 Sep post dates the deaths here to 27 Sep.)
Hills round Ti Zit collapse, burying the village's streets and the hill road out.
First slide at Kayin Gyi.
Water starts rising at Way Di; the road to Kone Zayat goes nearly 5 ft under and about 20 cattle are swept away.
Families in low-lying Launglon homes move out in the dark.
Inwa hill slides onto the monastery at Thea Pon.
Water starts entering houses in Kin Shey; by dawn the ground floors are under.
Second slide at Kayin Gyi; nearly 30 houses buried.
Water starts entering wards of Dawei town.
Water enters Pa Kar Ri on the border road; residents start moving out.
Floods begin in the Taung Pyauk area.
Rescue teams are held at Ka Myaw Gyi by floodwater; four red-level villages are out of reach.
Poe Zar Pin hill collapses onto the road between Launglon and Nyin Maw.
Rescue teams reach Tha Byar and clear slide debris.
Three bodies recovered in Launglon; tens missing. Slides continue on the western hills.
Mother's body recovered at Min Yat; her child is found alive.
Contact with Kyauk Ni Maw is lost.
The Poe Zar Pin slide stops the rescue convoy heading south.
Strong winds sweep Dawei District; the rain does not let up.
Slides at Pa Nyit bury two houses and cut the road either side of the village.
Water on the Dawei–Myeik road at Thin Kyun drops by about 2 ft.
Electricity is cut across the district's flooded areas.
Rescue teams still stuck at the slide; they appeal for backhoes and tractors.
DMH: 11.02 in (280 mm) of rain at Dawei, the highest on record. The old record, 9.68 in, dated from 1998.
Ten people, including elderly people and a child, rescued from rising water near Taik Thit monastery. Power is cut to the whole town.
Phone and internet lines go down across Tanintharyi Township.
Another slide buries the whole eastern half of Kayin Gyi.
Low-lying houses in Pa Kar Ri are completely submerged.
A landslide at Nyaw Pyin kills two women (reported on 28 Sep).
Residents of seven Dawei wards are moved out overnight to monasteries.
An advance rescue team leaves the road and walks round the slide through the forest.
Single-storey houses under water in five Dawei wards.
The advance team reaches Kadet Nge Htein and starts searching.
DMH: the low off the Tanintharyi coast may become a depression within 24 hours, moving north and north-west towards the Ayeyarwady delta.
No contact with Nyaw Pyin: phone and internet are down.
At least five bodies recovered in Launglon; dozens still missing. Rescuers have not reached Kadet Nge [Htein], Ti Zit or Za Lut.
The Ka Nyin Chaung bridge on Union Road No. 8 is destroyed; the Dawei–Myeik road is cut.
The rest of the rescue force is still clearing earth from the Launglon–Nyin Maw road.
Rain stops over Dawei, Launglon and most other places; the water starts to fall.
After three days of rain, villages on the Tanintharyi River begin to flood.
The rescue team has got no further than Auk Yay Phyu; villages to the south have had no help.
The Zambu Thiri team recovers the bodies of a 12-year-old boy and a monk; five dead at Kadet Nge Htein.
Water falls in Thayetchaung; the clean-up of mud and fallen trees begins.
Dawei Watch's Launglon count reaches nine dead; dozens missing.
The bodies of a mother and son are found under slide earth in their orchard at Kadet Gyi.
Water falls in Launglon town, Ka Myaw Gyi, Way Di, Min Yat and Tha Byar.
DMH: 13.62 in (346 mm) of rain at Dawei, beating the day-old record.
Six dead in Thayetchaung Township and two swept away.
The Launglon count reaches twelve dead.
Water falls in Dawei's wards; the sun comes out and people go home to clean up.
A mother and son at Tha Byar are still missing after three days.
Backhoes have cleared the road as far as Nyin Maw; Kyauk Ni Maw is days away.
Dawei Watch counts 23 dead in three townships (15 in Launglon, 6 in Thayetchaung, 2 in Dawei), with dozens missing.
Dawei town has now had no electricity since 27 Sep.
The Tanintharyi River passes 26 ft, over 2 ft above its 24 ft danger mark.
5 ft of water on the Tanintharyi–Kawthoung road; motorcycles cross on rafts.

quotes.by: Kyauk Ni Maw resident, a man, 26 Sep
quotes.mm: အိမ်တွေ လမ်းတွေ မြေဖုံးကုန်ပြီ။ အသက်ကြီး တစ်ယောက်ကိုလည်း ကျွန်တော်တို့ သွားခေါ်ထုတ်ထားတယ်။ မြေဖုံးနေတဲ့ ကလေး နှစ်ယောက်ကိုလည်း လောလောဆယ် ကယ်ထုတ်ထားတယ်။ မြေကအခုအထိ ဆက်ပြိုနေတုန်း အရေးပေါ်အကူအညီတွေ လိုနေတယ်
quotes.en: Houses and roads are buried. We went and brought out an old person, and we've pulled out two children who were buried. The ground is still collapsing. We need emergency help.

quotes.by: Sit Pyay resident, 26 Sep
quotes.mm: တစ်ရွာလုံးလည်း ပင်လယ်ပြင်ကြီးလိုဖြစ်သွားပြီ။ လူတွေလည်း ညမအိပ်ရဲကြဘူး။ တောင်ပြိုမှာကြောက်နေကြတယ်
quotes.en: The whole village has turned into an open sea. People don't dare sleep at night. They're afraid of landslides.

quotes.by: Kadet Nge [Htein] resident, 27 Sep
quotes.mm: သေတဲ့သူတွေ မနည်းဘူး။ နှစ်လောင်းပဲ ထုတ်လို့ရသေးတယ်
quotes.en: So many are dead. We've only been able to bring out two bodies.

quotes.by: Zambu Thiri rescue team member, 27 Sep
quotes.mm: ဒါကြောင့် ပိတ်မိနေတဲ့ မြေကြီးကိုပဲတူးပြီး ကျွန်တော်တို့ ဆက်သွားဖို့ စီစဉ်နေတယ်။ ဘက်ဟိုးတွေလည်း အကူအညီတောင်းထားတယ်
quotes.en: So we're planning to dig through the earth that's blocking us and carry on. We've asked for backhoes too.

quotes.by: Kin Shey resident, a woman, 27 Sep
quotes.mm: တစ်သက်နဲ့တစ်ကိုယ် တစ်ခါမှ မမြင်ဖူးဘူး။ ကျွန်မတို့ရွာမှာ ရေတက်လာလည်း ဒူးဆစ်လောက်ပဲ တက်ဖူးတယ်။ အခုက လူတစ်ရပ်လောက်အထိ မြုပ်တယ်။
quotes.en: I've never seen anything like it in my life. When water rose in our village it only ever came up to the knee. Now it's over a person's height.

quotes.by: Thin Kyun resident, a man, 3:30 pm 27 Sep
quotes.en: Big vehicles can get through, but it's hard for small cars and motorbikes. Now (3:30 pm) the water has dropped about two feet.

quotes.by: Taung Pyauk area resident, 27 Sep
quotes.en: The people are safe. But we've lost buffalo and cattle.

quotes.by: Kyauk Maw ward resident, Dawei, 27 Sep
quotes.mm: ရေမဝင်တဲ့နေရာ မရှိတော့ဘူး။ ရေဝင်နည်းတာနဲ့ ရေဝင်များတာပဲကွာတယ်။ အရင်က ရေမဝင်ဖူးတဲ့နေရာတွေတောင် ခြေမျက်စိနားလောက် ရေရောက်နေတယ်
quotes.en: There's nowhere the water hasn't got in. The only difference is how much. Even places that never flooded have water up to the ankle.

quotes.by: Dawei resident, morning of 28 Sep
quotes.mm: လျှပ်စစ်မီးလည်း မလာသေးဘူး ။ မိုးလည်းရွာနေသေးတယ် ။ ညကထက်စာရင်တော့ မိုးရွာ နည်းနည်းလျော့တယ် ။ ညက တစ်ညလုံးစိမ်ပြီး ရွာလိုက်တာ ရေအတိုးမြန်လို့ မအိပ်ဘဲစောင့်ကြည့်ခဲ့ရတယ်
quotes.en: Still no electricity, and it's still raining, a little less than last night. It poured all night and the water rose so fast we stayed up watching it.

quotes.by: Pa Kar Ri resident, night of 27 Sep
quotes.mm: မြေနိမ့်ပိုင်းတွေ လူအရပ် မမီတော့ဘူး
quotes.en: In the low-lying parts the water is over a person's head.

quotes.by: Kayin Gyi resident, a man, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: အရှေ့ပိုင်းတစ်ခြမ်းစာ မြေဖုံးသွားပြီး တံတားနားက လမ်းပိုင်းလည်း ပြတ်သွားတယ်
quotes.en: The whole eastern half is buried under earth, and the road by the bridge is cut.

quotes.by: Tha Kyet resident, Tanintharyi, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: ညကတည်းက ချောင်း‌‌ရေလျှံတယ်။ စမြုပ်နေပြီ နည်းနည်းမြင့်တဲ့ အိမ်တွေလောက်ကျန်ပြီ
quotes.en: The stream has been overflowing since last night. It's going under; only the slightly higher houses are left.

quotes.by: Search-and-rescue official, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: ရှာဖွေ ကယ်ဆယ်ရေးတွေ စလုပ်နေပြီပေါ့နော်။ အခုအထိတော့ ပိတ်မိနေသူတွေကို ရှာဖွေတာတွေ လုပ်ဆောင်နေပါတယ်။ အသေးစိတ် စာရင်းအတိအကျတော့ တက်မလာ သေးဘူး
quotes.en: Search and rescue has started. We're still looking for the people who are trapped. We don't have an exact list yet.

quotes.by: DDMSC information officer, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: အကူအညီက လုံးဝမရသေးဘူး။ ထားဝယ်က ဆင်းလာကူညီတဲ့အဖွဲ့ကလည်း အောက်ရေဖြူအထိပဲ ရောက်သေးတယ်။ အောက်ဘက်ရွာတွေအထိ ရောက်အောင် အတော်ဆင်းရဦးမယ်။
quotes.en: There's been no help at all. The team that came down from Dawei has only got as far as Auk Yay Phyu. It'll take a lot to reach the villages further south.

quotes.by: Way Di resident, a man, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: လမ်းမမှာ ရေက နည်းနည်းပဲကျန်ပြီ။ လယ်ထဲတော့ ရှိသေးတယ်။ ဝါးတင်တဲ့ ထော်လာဂျီတွေ သွားနေကြပြီ
quotes.en: There's only a little water left on the road. The fields are still flooded. The tractors carrying bamboo are moving again.

quotes.by: Myat Parami charity member, Thayetchaung, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: ကိုယ့်မြို့ထဲမှာ ဖြစ်နေတာကို ကိုယ်မကယ်နိုင်ဘဲ ဖြစ်နေတယ်။ အဓိကတော့ လှေမရှိတဲ့ဒဏ်ပေါ့။
quotes.en: It's happening in our own town and we can't rescue people. Above all, we have no boats.

quotes.by: Kyar Inn resident, a woman, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: တစ်ရွာလုံးက အထဲမှာ ပိတ်မိနေကြတာပါရှင်။ တစ်ယောက်မှ ထွက်မရဘူး
quotes.en: The whole village is trapped inside. Not one person can get out.

quotes.by: Villager who dug out the bodies, Kadet Gyi, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: ဒီနေ့မှ သူတို့ခြံထဲ ဝင်ရှာကြတာ ခြံတစ်ခြံလုံးက တောင်ပြိုမြေတွေနဲ့ ပြည့်နေပြီ အလောင်းကို မနည်းဖော်ထုတ်လာရတယ်
quotes.en: Only today could we go into their orchard to look. The whole orchard was full of slide earth; it took a lot to dig the bodies out.

quotes.by: U Naing Myo Thwin, Tanintharyi Region emergency rescue team, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: စပြီး ကယ်ထုတ်လာကတည်းက တချို့က အဝတ်အထည်တွေ ယူချိန်မရတဲ့သူတွေ ရှိတယ်။
quotes.en: Since we started bringing people out, some of them had no time to take any clothes.

quotes.by: Kadet Nge Htein resident, 28 Sep
quotes.en: Thirty-one houses completely destroyed. The earth covers about five football pitches in all.

quotes.by: Lay Hnya resident, a man, 28 Sep
quotes.mm: မိုးကအခုခဏပြတ်နေပေမဲ့ ဆက်ရွာရင် ရေဆက်လက်တက်လာနိုင်လို့ မြစ်ချောင်းနံဘေးနေထိုင်သူတွေအားလုံး ကြိုတင်ပြင်ပြီး သတိထားဖို့လိုလိမ့်မယ်
quotes.en: The rain has stopped for now, but if it starts again the water could keep rising, so everyone living by the rivers and streams needs to get ready and stay alert.

quotes.by: Nyaw Pyin resident, interviewed on the night of 28 Sep
quotes.mm: တောင်မပြိုခင်မှာ တောင်အော်တယ်လို့ သူကပြောပြတယ်။ လေယာဥ်ပျံအသံလိုမျိုး အသံကြမ်းတယ်ပေါ့။ တစ်ရွာလုံးဟိန်းသွားတယ်တဲ့။
quotes.en: He said the hill roared before it fell. A harsh sound, like an aeroplane. The whole village rang with it.

quotes.by: Neighbour of the missing mother and son, a woman, 29 Sep
quotes.mm: သူ့ဘဝလည်း သနားစရာ။ ထောင်ကနေ လွတ်လာတာ သုံးနှစ်တောင် မပြည့်သေးဘူး။ မိသားစုနဲ့ ပြန်ဆုံရတာ ခဏလေးပဲ ရှိသေးတယ်
quotes.en: His life is so sad. He's been out of prison less than three years; he'd only just got back to his family.

quotes.by: Tanintharyi Township resident, 29 Sep
quotes.mm: ရေက တက်လာတာ သုံးရက်အတွင်း တော်တော်မြန်တယ်။ ထားဝယ်ဘက်က ရေတွေ ဆင်းလာလို့လည်း ပါမယ်ထင်တယ်။
quotes.en: The water has come up very fast in three days. I think it's partly the water coming down from Dawei.

quotes.by: Tanintharyi town resident, 29 Sep
quotes.mm: ဒီမှာ မနေ့ကတည်းက မိုးတိတ်နေပေမဲ့ ထားဝယ်ဘက်က ရေဆင်းလာတော့ မြစ်ရေတိုးလာတာ
quotes.en: The rain stopped here yesterday, but the water coming down from the Dawei side is raising the river.

quotes.by: Kyauk Ni Maw villager coordinating aid from outside, 29 Sep
quotes.mm: ရွာထဲ ကျန်နေတဲ့လူတွေချည်းပဲ လက်နဲ့ ရှင်းလင်းရှာဖွေနေရတာပေါ့။ ဘက်ဟိုးလည်း မရှိ၊ ဘာယန္တရားမှလည်း မရှိ
quotes.en: It's only the people left in the village clearing and searching, by hand. No backhoe, no machinery at all.

quotes.by: Ti Zit resident, 29 Sep
quotes.mm: အခု တာဝါတိုင်မှာရှိနေတဲ့ ဆီကုန်ရင် ဆက်သွယ်ရေးလည်း ရတော့မှာ မဟုတ်ဘူး။ လောလောဆယ်တော့ ရွာက ဈေးဆိုင်တွေမှာ ရှိတဲ့ ရိက္ခာတွေနဲ့ပဲ စားနေသောက်နေကြရပါတယ်။ ဒါကုန်ရင် မရှိတော့ဘူး
quotes.en: When the fuel at the phone tower runs out, we'll lose contact too. For now we're living on what the village shops had. When that's gone, there's nothing.
